title: Circuit-breaker misfire during multi-region surge causes tenant request blackholing and silent 5xxs
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Summary:
During a sustained multi-region surge test on hosted + dedicated routing we observed a cascade where the circuit-breaker intended to protect overloaded backend pools incorrectly tripped for a subset of tenants, causing their traffic to be blackholed into a local rejection path that returned internal 5xxs (not the expected 429s). Affected customers reported sudden error spikes and degraded availability across Hosted and Dedicated deployments; Private customers running federated control planes saw similar symptoms during orchestrator failover.

What happened (high-level):
- A surge in cross-region traffic triggered the fanout heuristic in the routing layer.
- Circuit-breaker evaluation used stale tenant-rate metadata (cache TTL mismatch) and computed an out-of-date success ratio, deciding to open breakers for healthy tenants.
- Opened breakers routed to a 'degraded' engine that had a rare bug: instead of returning graceful 429s or queueing, it replied with 500-series errors and dropped KV cache usage headers, preventing transparent fallback.
- The orchestrator then attempted a reactive reroute; quota reconciliation logic saw repeated 5xxs as service failure and aggressively reallocated credits to other pools, producing a feedback loop that starved the originally healthy tenants.

Impact:
- Multiple premium Hosted customers and several Dedicated customers experienced sustained elevated error rates for 6-18 minutes during the incident window.
- Silent failures in Private deployments during orchestrator leader switch for customers using the federated control plane (no obvious alerts at customer side).
- Regressed token-level accounting and caused billing anomalies (intermittent double-counting warnings in cost dashboards).

Initial mitigation performed:
- Rolled back the new fanout weight heuristic (PR #https://github.com/redwood-inc/route-core/pull/4892) and reinstated conservative TTL for tenant-rate metadata cache (config flag: routing.tenant_cache_ttl_s = 30s).
- Deployed hotfix to the degraded engine to return 429s with structured retry-after and preserve KV-cache headers (PR #https://github.com/redwood-inc/runtime/pull/5127).
- Manually rebalanced credits and ran a reconciliation script to correct ledger inconsistencies for affected tenants (internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Rate+Incident+Runbook).

Root cause analysis (in-progress):
- Primary: cache invalidation mismatch between routing fanout code and tenant-rate updater leading to stale success/failure ratios used by circuit-breaker logic.
- Secondary: degraded-engine regression where fallback path used wrong response code path and cleared downstream metadata headers.
- Tertiary: orchestrator credits logic treated 5xxs as permanent service failure in fast-path reconciliation, which amplified the outage by moving credits away.

Acceptance criteria / definition of done:
- Fix deployed that ensures circuit-breaker calculations always reference authoritative tenant-rate state or a guaranteed-atomic snapshot.
- Degraded fallback path returns correct 429s and preserves KV/cache headers for fallback routing.
- Orchestrator credit reconciliation treats transient 5xxs as soft-fail (backoff) for 90s before hard reallocation.
- End-to-end test covering surge->fanout->circuit-breaker->fallback behavior with simulated TTL skew added to CI and smoke tests.
- Post-deploy synthetic monitors show no regression for 72h and affected tenants confirm return to normal.

Planned work:
1) Short term (P0 hotfix, under rollout):
   - Patch routing to read tenant-rate snapshot from shared revisioned state store (ENG-198766 will track a backing store change).
   - Revert fanout weight tweak and increase telemetry around stale-cache detections.
   - Roll out degraded-engine hotfix to Hosted + Dedicated + Private (canary to 1 region -> global).
2) Mid term (P1 follow-ups):
   - Add a circuit-breaker simulation test harness to validate logic under TTL skew and multi-region stale reads.
   - Improve orchestrator reconciliation policy to use graded backoff and annotate reallocation actions in audit logs.
3) Long term (P2):
   - Replace ad-hoc cache with versioned epoched metadata store with atomic read semantics for routing decisions.
   - Add SLA-aligned alerting and tenant-side webhook notifications for circuit open events.

Dependencies:
- ENG-198766 (tenant-rate epoched store prototype)
- ENG-198770 (orchestrator reconciliation policy revamp)

Notes / open questions:
- We need to decide if the degraded-engine fallback should be allowed to return 429-only for premium tenants to protect SLAs, or keep 500 fallback for internal metrics visibility. PM and CS prefer 429s to reduce customer incidents.
- Billing ledger correction requires finance sign-off for retroactive crediting for affected customers. Ops has prepared a csv of affected tenant ids and delta; finance owner: Priya Menon.

Runbook links and artifacts:
- Incident timeline + initial alert doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/2025-02-18-routing-circuit-breaker
- Hotfix PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inc/runtime/pull/5127, https://github.com/redwood-inc/route-core/pull/4892
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-198765+Postmortem

Next immediate steps (this week):
- Finish implement snapshot read for tenant-rate and QA (owner: Kieran) — target 2025-03-03 for canary.
- Run synthetic surge test with TTL mismatch scenarios (owner: SRE team) — target 2025-03-04.
- Update customer support notes and notify affected customers of corrective crediting timeline (owner: CS lead Maya Rodriguez) — target 2025-03-02.
